validity.recommendation: Verify/reclassify PipelineType. SemGroup's own SEC disclosures call this a gathering line, not transmission -- confirm current PipelineType and consider whether a 200 MMcf/d firm-committed intrastate takeaway line still belongs in this bucket the way GGIT scopes gathering vs. transmission elsewhere (same question already flagged on P2041 Taproot Baja/Rattlesnake in this batch).
validity.researcher_notes: SemGroup Corp's own SEC 10-K filings for BOTH FY2017 (filed 2018-02-26, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1489136/000148913618000004/semg1231201710-k.htm) and FY2018 (filed 2019-02-28, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1489136/000148913619000011/semg1231201810-k.htm) describe the asset identically, verbatim across both years: 'a 53-mile, high pressure gathering pipeline (the "Canton pipeline"), located in the STACK play with a capacity of 200 million cubic feet per day and backed by firm commitments from an investment-grade counterparty.' This is the pipeline's own owner/operator classifying it as a GATHERING line in an audited public filing, not transmission. Countervailing context: EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook labels it 'Intrastate' under 'Pipeline Type' (a jurisdictional category, not the gathering/transmission distinction) and notes it provides 'Takeaway capacity out of Anadarko basin' -- i.e. it functions as a basin egress/trunk line even if SemGroup's own accounting classifies the facility as gathering-grade. This is a genuine, sourced tension worth a human classification call, not a unilateral reclassification -- flagging rather than changing PipelineType outright.

validity.recommendation: Verify LengthKnown -- SemGroup's own 10-K (both FY2017 and FY2018) states 53 miles, not the 50 miles recorded on the sheet (which traces to the original 2017 project announcement).
validity.researcher_notes: The recorded LengthKnown=50 mi traces to SemGroup's 2017-05-03 project announcement ('approximately 50 miles' -- GlobeNewswire, and the same figure was picked up by the Oklahoma Minerals trade-press piece and, evidently, by EIA's workbook, which also cites a SemGroup investor deck as its source). But SemGroup's own AUDITED SEC 10-K filings -- for FY2017 (filed Feb 2018) AND independently restated in FY2018 (filed Feb 2019) -- both describe it as 'a 53-mile ... pipeline.' A consistent as-built figure in two consecutive audited annual reports from the pipeline's own owner is likely more authoritative than a pre-construction press estimate of 'approximately 50 miles.' Flagging as a material (6%) discrepancy rather than silently keeping 50 or silently overwriting to 53 -- see the paired Length [ref] fill below, which stages 53 mi as the corrected/proposed value with both 10-Ks as refs.

That is not what the record shows: SemGroup Corp's own 10-Ks (FY2017, FY2018) name Canton as a SemGroup-owned/operated asset through year-end 2018, and Energy Transfer LP's investor-relations press release of 2019-12-05 (verified via Wayback; https://ir.energytransfer.com/news-releases/news-release-details/energy-transfer-and-semgroup-announce-successful-completion) announces the SEPARATE, EARLIER completion of the Energy Transfer/SemGroup Corp merger -- 'the completion of their previously announced merger, which resulted in the acquisition of Tulsa-based SemGroup by Dallas-based Energy Transfer,' explicitly covering SemGroup's Anadarko Basin (Oklahoma) gas gathering/processing assets. That release does not name 'Canton' specifically (so it is not itself a valid stand-alone ref for the Owner cell per the naming rule -- see the paired Owner [ref] fill), but combined with the two 10-Ks it establishes SemGroup->Energy Transfer, Dec 2019, as the correct chain for this specific asset -- two years before the Enable merger the brief points to. Recommend the current-batch docs cite the SemGroup 2019 merger for Canton, and reserve the Enable/2021 merger note for P2560/P0376.
